title: Zod Validation
description: Schema validation for forms and API payloads.

data.text: Zod schemas can validate form inputs and provide TypeScript types simultaneously.

data.title: Zod with React Hook Form

data.text: One Schema for Client and Server

This lesson is about using Zod as the validation layer rather than about the library itself. The same schema can validate a form in the browser and the body of an API request on the server, so a rule is defined once and enforced on both sides — the client for feedback, the server for truth.

data.title: A shared schema across the boundary

data.text: `error.flatten()` groups issues by field name, which maps directly onto form inputs. Cross-field rules such as a confirm-password or an end-after-start date use `.refine` with a `path` so the message lands on the right field. `.partial()` and `.pick()` derive smaller schemas from a base one.

data.title: Cross-field rules and derived schemas
never trust the client
data.text: Client-side validation is a convenience for the user; the server must validate again because a request can be sent without ever loading the page. The pattern to present is a shared schema module, a client resolver that gives instant feedback, and a server parse that is the authoritative check. Saying only the first half is a common and costly interview mistake.
